definitions.explanation: A large organized event, typically involving music, arts, food, or cultural activities. Often used for Western-style or modern festivals rather than traditional Japanese ones.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}のフェスティバルに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to a summer festival.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}フェスティバルで{新作|しんさく}が{上映|じょうえい}された。
examples.english: A new film was screened at the film festival.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{秋|あき}に{開催|かいさい}される{音楽|おんがく}フェスティバルには{全国|ぜんこく}から{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まる。
examples.english: People gather from all over the country for the music festival held every autumn.

notes:
Borrowed from English "festival." Often shortened to フェス in casual speech, especially for music festivals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {音楽|おんがく}フェスティバル (music festival)
- {映画|えいが}フェスティバル (film festival)
- フードフェスティバル (food festival)
- フェスティバルに{参加|さんか}する (to participate in a festival)
- フェスティバルを{開催|かいさい}する (to hold a festival)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- フェスティバル / フェス: modern, often Western-style events (music festivals, art festivals)
- {祭|まつ}り: traditional Japanese festivals (shrines, processions, {盆踊|ぼんおど}り)
- イベント: broader term for any organized event

The abbreviated form フェス is very common in casual speech, especially among younger speakers: {夏|なつ}フェス (summer music festival), {野外|やがい}フェス (outdoor festival).

cross_references.label: broader term for any organized event
